_comment: The status-check contexts that must block a merge into main, and the
PR-triggered jobs deliberately exempted from blocking. This file is the
in-tree mirror of the `main` ruleset's required_status_checks; the ruleset
itself lives in repo settings, where nothing in the tree can see it.
tests/repo/test_required_status_checks.py pins all three parties to each
other: every context here must name a real job, every PR-triggered job must
be required or listed in `exempt` with a reason, and — wherever an
authenticated `gh` can reach the API — this list must equal what the live
ruleset actually enforces. Editing this file without editing the ruleset
A context is matched by the job's `name:` string, so renaming a job here
and in the workflow but not in the ruleset leaves a check that still runs
and still reports green while no longer blocking anything.

exempt.Eval live regression (opt-in): Dispatches the real agents and costs model tokens. Runs only behind a 'run-eval' label plus ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and skips (not fails) without them — a required check would report success on every PR that didn't opt in.
exempt.Eval integration tier (opt-in): Same opt-in posture as the live gate: real orchestrator dispatch, real tokens, label-gated.
exempt.Stryker.NET POSIX signal tests: Path-filtered to the mutation wrapper. A path-filtered workflow reports NO status on PRs that don't match, so requiring it would deadlock every unrelated PR at 'Waiting for status to be reported'.
exempt.PMD checksum verify: Path-filtered to the PMD installer + its checksum verifier (plus the shared weekly schedule). Same deadlock shape as the Stryker.NET signal tests above — a path-filtered workflow reports no status on unrelated PRs.
exempt.Orchestrator real-subprocess test: Schedule and workflow_dispatch only — it shells out to the real `claude` CLI, whose outcome, latency, and cost vary by host. It reports no status on a PR at all.
exempt.Pytest on native Windows: Path-filtered to the mutation wrapper for cost reasons (Windows runners), so it reports no status on unrelated PRs — same deadlock as the Stryker.NET signal tests above.
